name: Back in Control / The DOC Journey (David Hanscom)
founders: David Hanscom, MD (orthopedic spinal-deformity surgeon, Seattle; Loma Linda MD 1979; Twin Cities Scoliosis Center fellowship 1986; retired from surgery 2019)
founded_year_range: 2012 (Back in Control 1st ed., Vertus Press; approach used clinically from mid-2000s); DOC Journey online course 2020 (first Wayback capture of thedocjourney.com Sept 2020)
cost_summary: Oct 2026, USD (verified on checkout pages): Pre-Course $20 (1 month); DOC Journey course $25/mo after 14-day free trial; group coaching (Tue/Thu 12-1 pm PT Zoom) $72/mo; course+coaching bundle $87/mo; no partial refunds; flipbooks $3.99; books at retail price.
mechanisms: autonomic/nervous system dysregulation (sympathetic overdrive, "stuck in fight-or-flight")
neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
mechanism_summary: Hanscom calls the core state "threat physiology": a sustained "adrenalized" fight-or-flight state caused by inescapable pain or threat, life losses and repetitive unwanted thoughts. Through neuroplasticity, chronic pain shifts to emotional circuits and becomes coupled to stress and anger. His later writing adds inflammation, glial/immune signalling, mitochondrial dysfunction and reduced prefrontal blood flow. Mental and physical pain are treated as the same phenomenon. The course FAQ states verbatim: "Almost every chronic mental and physical illness and disease arises from sustained exposure to stress chemistry." Structural lesions are the only category triaged separately, for surgical or medical care.
techniques: Expressive writing: write negative thoughts, then destroy the paper immediately (daily)
Active meditation / sensory attention shifting, relaxation, breathing
Anger work, forgiveness, letting go of the victim role, dissolving ego/cognitive distortions
Self-paced video lessons, monthly webinars, app
mainstream_notes: Hanscom used a structured non-operative care pathway in his own spine practice (Seattle Neuroscience Specialists/Swedish Medical Center), but no outcome study was published. He chaired the Scoliosis Research Society non-operative care committee (2019), led its non-operative care standards manual, consulted for Premera Blue Cross (2006-2015) and has consulted for Spine Zone since 2021 (all per his bio). The ACPA 2020 Resource Guide listing and the Washington Bree Collaborative citation are claimed on his site but were not independently verified. No health-system, payer, NICE or CMS adoption of the DOC Journey course was found.
insurance_notes: Direct-to-consumer monthly subscriptions via Kajabi. Clinician-delivered CBT or PT along similar lines may be covered as usual care, but the program itself is not.

key_trials.citation: Hanscom DA, Brox JI, Bunnage R. Defining the role of cognitive behavioral therapy in treating chronic low back pain: an overview. Global Spine J 2015;5(6):496-504. PMID 26682100
key_trials.design: Narrative review (not a trial of the program)
key_trials.finding: Argues that CBT should be defined by the problem it targets and recommends early, widespread CBT for chronic low back pain. Contains no outcome data on DOC.

key_trials.citation: Salikka T, Kylmä J, Fröjd S, et al. Therapeutic writing interventions for adults with chronic pain: experiences and health effects. A systematic review with a narrative synthesis. Eur J Pain 2026. PMID 41699922
key_trials.design: Systematic review of generic therapeutic/expressive writing (NOT the DOC program)
key_trials.finding: Modest psychological benefits and inconsistent, short-lived physical effects. This is indirect evidence for the program's signature component, and it does not cover the write-and-destroy variant.

controversy: The claim that almost every chronic mental and physical illness stems from stress chemistry (course FAQ) is sweeping and unvalidated, and it is extended by theory alone to POTS, IBS, tinnitus, CRPS, eating disorders and PTSD. The signature "write and destroy" expressive-writing variant has never been tested. Efficacy claims ("over 1000 patients" freed from pain) are founder-reported and have no denominators. A PubMed check (32 records for Hanscom D) found no outcome study of the program. There is a mild conflict of interest: a former surgeon with strong credibility is marketing his own subscription. No regulatory actions were found, although the search was limited.

popularity.reach_estimate: About 10^4.5 (roughly 30,000). Basis: book readership for two editions and two later books, likely tens of thousands; patients seen clinically, >1,000 claimed; DOC subscribers inferred at hundreds to low thousands; plus podcast/blog audience. No official counts.
popularity.method_notes: Trajectory is anchored on documented milestones: books in 2012, around 2016 and 2019 plus the newest; Omega workshops around 2018; retirement from surgery in 2019; DOC Journey launch in 2020; Psychology Today column 2025-2026. Levels are within-program and relative. The web-search quota was exhausted during both research and fact-checking, so Reddit, Google Trends, Amazon/Goodreads and podcast metrics were not retrieved; levels are coarse judgments. Reach is an order-of-magnitude inference.
